tickets.title: Typography: a soft serif (Fraunces) for showcase headings, 16 px reading text, variable Figtree
tickets.scope:
The new site is set in Figtree only. It matches the lowercase geometric logo and reads well in SKUs, prices and tables, so it stays the base. What is missing is a voice where the customer is inspired, not working: the old site had serif headings (DM Serif Display), the new one has none.

Step 1 (stop for Roman): run `elme-look-options`. One page in `docs/design/`, phone and desktop, with the same real content (home hero, two home section titles, a Shop the Looks page, the collaboration landing, About us, and for contrast a PLP and a PDP header) in three looks: A Figtree only (today); B Fraunces for showcase headings; C Newsreader for showcase headings. Show for B and C a light and a regular weight and one italic accent. Do not edit templates in this step.

Step 2 after the pick: add the chosen family in `hyva.config.json` → `fonts` as `font-display` (one variable woff2, Latin subset, preloaded only where a showcase heading is above the fold) and a role token for it. Use it only for: hero titles, home section titles, lookbook and collaboration page titles, About / Style Sourcebook banners. Everything else stays Figtree: category and product names, H1 on PLP and PDP, menu, buttons, forms, tables, cart, checkout, account, prices and SKUs (tabular numerals).

Rule: serif where the customer is inspired, sans where the customer works. The type scale of UX-14 does not change; if a showcase size needs a different line height in the serif, add it to the role token, not to a template.

Two more changes in step 2:
- Reading text at 16 px: product descriptions, accordion text, help and content pages, FAQ answers use at least 16 px with line height 1.5 on phone and desktop (today the `copy` role is 14 px / 15 px). Change the role token, or point these places at the body role; dense UI (tables, cards, cart rows, labels) keeps its size.
- Figtree as one variable file: replace the four static weights and the separate `FigtreeHeading` family with one variable woff2 (Latin subset, preloaded); headings get their weight from the weight axis.
